column1: # Reviewed user-facing text for commits made without a "Changelog:" trailer (scripts/changelog.py).
# <sha>TAB<text, optionally "[Section] text">; "-" drops the commit.  UK spelling, our own words.
# A commit with a Changelog: trailer needs a line here only to correct it (a line wins over the trailer).

column2: Album covers no longer start over again when nothing has changed
Your library is built first: covers and other background work wait until it has finished
The library page says in plain words which step it is on, with a light that keeps moving
Full speed is held while a high-quality track plays
More FLAC files play: blocks of up to 65,535 samples are now supported
A queue in which nothing can play now stops instead of cycling through it
Shuffle no longer gets stuck on a very small library
[Playback and sound] FLAC files decode faster, most of all high-quality 24-bit ones
[Playback and sound] All music is now decoded on the player's second processor
[Playback and sound] FLAC, WAV and AIFF files recorded with more than 16 bits play at their full depth
[Playback and sound] Better-quality conversion for music that is not at 44.1 or 48 kHz
[Playback and sound] Some high-quality FLAC files that could play wrongly now play correctly
[Playback and sound] FLAC files wider than 29 bits are skipped cleanly instead of playing wrongly
[Power and start-up] The player watches both of its processors when it chooses its speed
[Playback and sound] Opus files need fewer hand-overs between the two processors when they start
[Playback and sound] When a song cannot be played, the next one now starts straight away
[Interface] Touching the wheel wakes the screen when it shows the clock face
[Storage and USB] One build for flash and hard-drive players: the player finds out which it has
[Power and start-up] The first start asks which battery is fitted
[Video] A video that cannot start stops the sound and shows a message instead of a blank screen

column1: # 0.9.0: B4 trailers named a section that does not exist ([Artwork])

column2: [Interface] A damaged cover picture can no longer corrupt memory when its album plays
[Interface] A damaged cover inside an Ogg or Opus file no longer leaves the player stuck working on it
Japanese text breaks between lines in the right places
Songs and audiobooks that can't play are greyed out with a small sign
Settings > Language switches between English, Deutsch and Nederlands at once
Menus in German and Dutch (first drafts)
Menus in Japanese (first draft)
The equaliser and other sound processing now run on the second core, with the decoding
After a seamless change of sample rate, the next song plays at its own speed
[Playback and sound] A stop during a change of sample rate no longer leaves the player waiting for a change that never comes
[Playback and sound] Fewer short drop-outs in demanding files while the second core tidies its memory
The audio chip is powered at 3.0 V, as in the original software, for a little more headroom
[Playback and sound] The Hi-Res 128x test plays a few seconds at each rate, including a near-silent stretch, and fails on the smallest break
Settings > Legal now credits the font used for Japanese, Korean and Chinese characters
[Playback and sound] A damaged Apple Lossless file now stops the track instead of writing past the decoder's memory
[Playback and sound] 24-bit Apple Lossless files now play at their full 24-bit precision; before, the lowest 8 bits were lost
[Video] A rare video-chip hiccup when switching between album art and the visualiser is fixed

[Playback and sound] With Hi-Res 128x on, music at 88.2 and 96 kHz now runs the audio chip's sound processing at full speed, which removes a faint crackle in quiet endings; the audio chip's limiter now guards the equaliser against sudden peaks
